traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 330 Geraniaceae: annual herbs or undershrubs, rarely tree-like; leaves alternate or opposite, mostly lobed, cut or compound; stipules often paired; flowers regular or slightly irregular (Pelargonium); sepals 4 or 5, petals 5, rarely 4; stamens two or three times the sepals; ovary of 3 to 5 lobes; fruit lobed, each lobe one-seeded, often beaked (the cranesbill's), read as a schizocarp. The ovary's superior place is the petals' 'hypogynous'.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Geraniaceae with Biebersteiniaceae, Dirachmaceae, Hypseocharitaceae, Ledocarpaceae, Vivianiaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
